tables.caption_tex: \textbf{LIBERO success rates (\%).} Across comparative tables, bold/underlining indicate the best/second-best values for each metric and setting, including ties. References retain published protocols; WLA-0 uses standard inference. Sources and status appear in Appendix~\ref{app:protocols}.

\textbf{RMBench success rates (\%).} TMC: task memory complexity; VA: visual anchors. Dashes indicate unavailable results. Reference protocols and reporting status are specified in Appendix~\ref{app:protocols}.

\textbf{Component comparisons (\%).} The upper block varies store access; the lower block tests source initialization and explicit comparison. Rankings span both blocks. Appendix~\ref{app:ablation_defs} provides definitions and run-attribution status for all six evaluated variants.

\textbf{Candidate-effect assessment.} Rows share states, proposals, and independent applicability labels. Bold/underlining mark best/second-best values; tie rate is diagnostic. Query-only ordering and ties are analytical; Appendix~\ref{app:effect_probes} details the metrics and coverage.

\textbf{From module inputs to control outputs.} Each row names the computation, its direct inputs, and its output's role. Demonstrated actions and futures supply training targets and corruption controls; the reads below use their stated context.
\textbf{Notation and module index.} Meanings, computational roles, and definition references for all seven groups.
\textbf{Simulation interfaces for \method{}.} Horizons and execution prefixes count model action steps. Baseline-specific observation and execution interfaces are described below.
\textbf{Sources of the published reference results.} Values retain source versions and protocols.
\textbf{Evaluated training and inference configuration.} \textsf{TBD} fields require the actual checkpoint and launch records; development-probe settings are reported separately.

tables.caption_tex: \textbf{Admission on independently labelled proposals (pending).} Labels come from the shared branches. Rates use deterministically eligible proposals and episode-clustered intervals.
\textbf{Measured candidate-withdrawal consistency.} Development checkpoint \texttt{v8-step300}; ten source episodes. The measurement concerns numerical output invariance at forced $g=0$.
\textbf{Same-information reuse comparison (pending).} One comparator, three predefined tasks. The last column is the matched three-task average, distinct from the full RMBench average.

\textbf{Measured source diagnostic at \texttt{v8-step300}.} Three independent source processes share 50 fixed prefixes. Zero active-gate coverage explains the identical outputs; a mature-checkpoint run is required to assess the contribution of recalled-action content under natural admission.
\textbf{Source-content control (pending).} Matched training/evaluation on two specified tasks. Report SR and realized gate/noise statistics; local probes hold gates fixed.
\textbf{Requirement-evidence control (pending).} One checkpoint and a fixed candidate branch set. Matched masks test whether critical history improves present assessment.

\textbf{Measured deployment-path cost on recorded development prefixes.} One H100 80GB, BF16, batch one; checkpoint \texttt{v8-step300}. Times are descriptive over 200 calls. Memory is the CUDA allocator's peak, including resident models and the online retrieval encoder.

figures.caption_tex:
\textbf{From interaction evidence to selective action reuse.}
(a,b) Illustrative WAM interfaces use local observations or retained history.
(c) Recollection grounds the task requirement; the repertoire supplies action--effect proposals.
Predicted consequence compatibility informs selection and a shared gate over source and conditioning.
K/V denotes visual keys and values; dashed arrows indicate training-only prediction.
\textbf{Right:} Benchmark results with published references (Tables~\ref{tab:libero}--\ref{tab:rmbench}) and distraction on Put Back Block and Press Button, averaged equally within each of five evaluation runs.

\textbf{From interaction evidence to generative action reuse.}
  Recollection $\mathcal M_t$ grounds a transition requirement $r_t$; repertoire actions are adapted into proposals $\mu_i$ and assessed through predicted effects $\widehat E_i$.
  A shared gate $g_t$ regulates the selected proposal in both initialization and conditioning, while executed actions and observations update recollection.
  The lower panels detail event construction, transition inference, and consequence-aligned recall; dashed arrows denote future-video prediction used only during training to retain predictive supervision.

\textbf{Robustness to inapplicable experience.} (a) Full \method{} and the no-comparison variant under three retrieval conditions on Put Back Block and Press Button. Curves average the two tasks across five evaluation runs (100 resets per task/run); bars show run-level SD. The dotted line is the recollection-only reference. (b) Drops from the same means. Appendix~\ref{app:distraction_protocol} specifies the intervention.
